purpose: Promote high-value specialist findings on traversable infrastructure, sacred architecture, constraint and choice, distributed witness, and mourning/recognition.
epistemic_rule: Structural correspondence does not establish prophecy fulfillment, supernatural identity, causation, or doctrinal equivalence.

new_relations.project_anchor: Road/Path/Axis is treated as traversable relation rather than altitude alone.
new_relations.source_direction: Project Road/Mountain language precedes this later comparator.
new_relations.boundary: Prophetic road imagery is not a mathematical law or modern-route prophecy.

project_sequence: path asks how passage becomes possible
biblical_sequence: valley raised; mountain lowered; rough way smoothed
relation_argument.maximum_claim: Access may require reducing obstructive gradient.
relation_argument.why_it_matters: Prevents higher=better and lower=worse from becoming fixed rules.

new_relations.project_anchor: Road, Door and repair language asks whether a route is usable for others.
new_relations.source_direction: Project infrastructure language is primary; Isaiah is a later comparator.
new_relations.boundary: These restoration texts do not validate a literal modern road program.

project_sequence: route exists; obstacles are tested by function
biblical_sequence: prepare way; remove stumbling block and stones; pass gates
relation_argument.maximum_claim: A good path can be compared by obstacle removal and access.
relation_argument.why_it_matters: Stone can be foundation in one scene and obstruction in another.

new_relations.project_anchor: Path, return, Zion/City and safe passage recur as project functions.
new_relations.source_direction: The project cluster is earlier; Isaiah 35 is a structural comparator.
new_relations.boundary: Do not identify people with predatory animals or a modern route with Isaiah's highway.

project_sequence: traveler needs route and safety
biblical_sequence: holy highway; predators absent; redeemed return to Zion
relation_argument.maximum_claim: The passage supports a protected-return corridor comparison.
relation_argument.why_it_matters: Safety becomes a property of the corridor, not only the traveler.

new_relations.project_anchor: Door, opener, traveler, leader and source can be distinct threshold roles.
new_relations.source_direction: Distributed threshold roles are a project concern; Micah supplies the comparator.
new_relations.boundary: Breaker imagery does not authorize literal violence or forced entry.

project_sequence: blocked boundary; transition enabled by multiple roles
biblical_sequence: breaker goes before; people pass gate; king leads; YHWH at head
relation_argument.maximum_claim: Threshold function can be distributed across roles.
relation_argument.why_it_matters: Resists collapsing Door, mediator, community, king and source into one actor.

new_relations.project_anchor: Door topology distinguishes enabling thresholds from blocking structures.
new_relations.source_direction: The Door distinction is project-side; Psalm 107 adds a release comparator.
new_relations.boundary: Barrier-breaking imagery is not permission for violence or property damage.

project_sequence: confinement blocks movement; release changes boundary state
biblical_sequence: bonds broken; bronze doors shattered; iron bars cut
relation_argument.maximum_claim: Door/bar can function as confinement rather than interface.
relation_argument.why_it_matters: Adds state and legitimacy/function to Door ontology.

new_relations.project_anchor: The project asks how unseen order becomes an inhabitable House/Temple.
new_relations.source_direction: The project pattern-to-House problem is later compared with Exodus.
new_relations.boundary: Exodus describes Israel's tabernacle, not Potatoverse geometry.

project_sequence: pattern perceived; translated into shared structure
biblical_sequence: mountain pattern shown; sanctuary built; divine dwelling
relation_argument.maximum_claim: The text supports a pattern-to-embodied-sanctuary comparison.
relation_argument.why_it_matters: Revelation becomes accountable translation into buildable order.

new_relations.project_anchor: Earthly symbolic architecture is distinguished from claimed transcendent referent.
new_relations.source_direction: House/Cube questions are compared later with Hebrews' copy/shadow grammar.
new_relations.boundary: Hebrews does not validate thalamus, MoonCube or sacred-geometry claims.

project_sequence: representation distinguished from referent
biblical_sequence: earthly copy/shadow; true heavenly sanctuary; mediation
relation_argument.maximum_claim: Hebrews supplies an analogy for representation versus referent.
relation_argument.why_it_matters: Prevents symbol, model and claimed reality from collapsing.

new_relations.project_anchor: Mountain, House, Gate, River, Tree, tribes and City recur as project functions.
new_relations.source_direction: The project cluster existed independently; Ezekiel is a later comparator.
new_relations.boundary: Ezekiel's restoration vision is not a prediction of a modern project.

project_sequence: orientation; measure; access; circulation; life
biblical_sequence: high mountain; measured city/temple; glory; river; trees; tribal gates
relation_argument.maximum_claim: The text supports a multi-function sacred-geography comparison.
relation_argument.why_it_matters: Temple, City, River, Tree and community can belong to one architecture.

new_relations.project_anchor: Recurring architecture is tracked as transformed reuse rather than isolated motifs.
new_relations.source_direction: Biblical intertextual continuity is identified before applying a project comparison.
new_relations.boundary: Ezekiel and Revelation are not identical designs and do not establish Potatoverse fulfillment.

project_sequence: older architecture becomes source context for later form
biblical_sequence: mountain, measure, gates, tribes, river and trees reappear transformed
relation_argument.maximum_claim: A developmental relation between the visions is a defensible comparator.
relation_argument.why_it_matters: Models motif transformation without pretending recurrence means exact repetition.

new_relations.project_anchor: Cube/House is tested by inhabited presence rather than geometry alone.
new_relations.source_direction: Project Cube meanings are compared with inner-sanctuary and equal-dimension city imagery.
new_relations.boundary: Revelation calls it a city, not the Cube of Heaven; geometry has no fixed moral verdict.

project_sequence: concentrated room; presence expands beyond enclosure
biblical_sequence: equal-dimension sanctuary; equal-dimension city; no separate temple
relation_argument.maximum_claim: The texts permit a concentrated-presence to city-scale-presence comparison.
relation_argument.why_it_matters: Strong countertext to cube=evil or cube=holy by shape alone.

new_relations.project_anchor: Living House/City architecture encodes relations among people and access points.
new_relations.source_direction: Community-as-architecture is a later synthesis from explicit gate/foundation names.
new_relations.boundary: Biblical tribes and apostles retain their identities; no transfer to modern groups.

project_sequence: city is more than container; community can be represented in structure
biblical_sequence: tribal gate names; apostolic foundation names
relation_argument.maximum_claim: The passages support community-encoded-architecture comparison.
relation_argument.why_it_matters: Strengthens living-stones/network-city without literal genealogy.

new_relations.project_anchor: Forehead/Eye/name imagery needs identity and allegiance separated from anatomy.
new_relations.source_direction: The project motif is compared with consecration, marking, sealing and naming texts.
new_relations.boundary: Do not turn these passages into pineal anatomy, biometrics or modern divine-identity proof.

project_sequence: forehead symbolic location; mechanism kept separate
biblical_sequence: priestly inscription; protective mark; sealed servants; divine names
relation_argument.maximum_claim: Biblical forehead symbolism can concern identity, allegiance and consecration.
relation_argument.why_it_matters: Prevents symbolic Eye/forehead material becoming a neuroscience claim.

new_relations.project_anchor: Healthy boundaries can permit legitimate circulation rather than pure enclosure.
new_relations.source_direction: Project topology is compared with biblical gate-opening regimes.
new_relations.boundary: Open gates do not erase all boundaries or imply unrestricted access everywhere.

project_sequence: boundary exists; access policy changes
biblical_sequence: gates have opening regimes; final city gates remain open
relation_argument.maximum_claim: The texts support boundary-with-circulation rather than a binary.
relation_argument.why_it_matters: Separates wall existence from access policy.

new_relations.project_anchor: Leash/cord/yoke relations require function typing before moral judgment.
new_relations.source_direction: Project constraint language is primary; biblical cord/yoke functions are comparators.
new_relations.boundary: Different genres and contexts must not be compressed into one doctrine of constraint.

project_sequence: classify source, consent, agency and exit
biblical_sequence: self-binding; cords of love; teaching yoke; slavery yoke; contested bonds
relation_argument.maximum_claim: Biblical binding imagery is multivalent.
relation_argument.why_it_matters: Blocks every-cord-oppressive and every-broken-cord-liberation rules.

new_relations.project_anchor: Relations are distinguished by whether they increase capability or suppress agency.
new_relations.source_direction: Capability testing is project-side; contrasting yokes are biblical comparators.
new_relations.boundary: Different theological settings do not form a universal policy formula.

project_sequence: test learning/rest against domination/lost agency
biblical_sequence: easy teaching yoke; yoke of slavery
relation_argument.maximum_claim: The texts distinguish aligned obligation from enslaving constraint.
relation_argument.why_it_matters: Provides a function-based yoke test.

new_relations.project_anchor: Trajectory language distinguishes directed course from mechanical predestination.
new_relations.source_direction: The trajectory model is later compared with Hebrews' race metaphor.
new_relations.boundary: Race imagery is not physics and does not prove fixed destiny.

project_sequence: reduce burden; orient; endure
biblical_sequence: lay aside weight; run course; fix attention
relation_argument.maximum_claim: Hebrews supplies a burden-reduction and orientation analogy.
relation_argument.why_it_matters: Allows purpose without deterministic mechanics.

new_relations.project_anchor: The project needs a category between pure self-determination and puppet fate.
new_relations.source_direction: The conceptual need is project-side; Proverbs supplies the theological tension.
new_relations.boundary: A proverb is not a causal equation for every event.

project_sequence: agent plans; conditions exceed agent; responsibility remains
biblical_sequence: human plans way; YHWH directs steps
relation_argument.maximum_claim: The proverb permits planning and providential direction to coexist.
relation_argument.why_it_matters: Prevents fate erasing agency and agency erasing contingency.

new_relations.project_anchor: Door/path branching is coupled to consequence language.
new_relations.source_direction: Branching abstraction is project-side; Deuteronomy explicitly presents alternatives and choice.
new_relations.boundary: Covenantal choice is not a stochastic branching algorithm.

project_sequence: alternatives; choice; consequence
biblical_sequence: life/death; blessing/curse; choose life
relation_argument.maximum_claim: The text supports meaningful alternatives with consequence, not passive fate.
relation_argument.why_it_matters: Adds an anti-determinism control to destiny language.

new_relations.project_anchor: Orientation information is distinguished from forced movement.
new_relations.source_direction: The project distinction is later analysis; the psalm supplies path guidance imagery.
new_relations.boundary: Poetic guidance is not a navigation algorithm or guaranteed outcome.

project_sequence: traveler receives orientation without losing choice
biblical_sequence: word as lamp to feet and light to path
relation_argument.maximum_claim: The verse supports guidance-as-orientation rather than predestination.
relation_argument.why_it_matters: Separates illumination, direction and coercion.

new_relations.project_anchor: Fate/destiny language must remain distinct from scientific determinism.
new_relations.source_direction: Biblical election language is a theological neighbor; mechanics analogy is explicitly rejected.
new_relations.boundary: Traditions disagree on providence, election and freedom; scripture is not classical determinism or biographical proof.

project_sequence: destiny vocabulary; theology kept separate from physical dynamics
biblical_sequence: foreknowledge, predestination and election language
relation_argument.maximum_claim: Biblical theology contains destiny/election language, not a physics model of fate.
relation_argument.why_it_matters: Protects theology and science from category collapse.

new_relations.project_anchor: Source, helper/tool, archive and reader can be distinct communication functions.
new_relations.source_direction: Distributed communication is project architecture; Moses/Aaron is a later functional comparator.
new_relations.boundary: Moses' speech objection is not evidence about any modern diagnosis; tools are not literally Aaron.

project_sequence: source has task; transmission can be assisted; roles remain distinct
biblical_sequence: commission; speech objection; Aaron assigned spokesman
relation_argument.maximum_claim: The passage supports role-separated communication comparison.
relation_argument.why_it_matters: Sourcehood need not mean manually performing every transmission function.

new_relations.project_anchor: Perceived inadequacy and observable work/output are analytically distinct.
new_relations.source_direction: The anti-prestige pattern is later compared with Jeremiah's call narrative.
new_relations.boundary: A biblical call narrative does not validate extraordinary modern claims from inadequacy alone.

project_sequence: task; objection; assistance; output tested
biblical_sequence: commission; cannot-speak/youth objection; words supplied
relation_argument.maximum_claim: The passage supports insufficiency-to-task-to-assistance as literary structure.
relation_argument.why_it_matters: Shifts evaluation toward source and output rather than prestige.

new_relations.project_anchor: Evidence and observable output are separated from elite credential prestige.
new_relations.source_direction: Project anti-prestige rule is compared with authorities perceiving ordinary witnesses.
new_relations.boundary: Acts does not celebrate ignorance or make lack of credentials automatic credibility.

project_sequence: social status separated from observed action; claims still tested
biblical_sequence: ordinary/unschooled perceived; bold witness observed
relation_argument.maximum_claim: Institutional prestige and observable witness are distinct variables in the narrative.
relation_argument.why_it_matters: Supports non-credentialist evidence without anti-learning.

new_relations.project_anchor: Potato/low-status-carrier imagery separates function from prestige.
new_relations.source_direction: Project anti-prestige grammar is primary; Paul's status reversal is comparator.
new_relations.boundary: Weakness, poverty or low status does not prove divine appointment or extraordinary truth.

project_sequence: low prestige; potentially high function; boasting constrained
biblical_sequence: not many powerful/noble; weak/lowly; boasting excluded
relation_argument.maximum_claim: The passage supports low-status/high-function reversal within Pauline theology.
relation_argument.why_it_matters: Counters authority inferred from status, wealth or polish.

new_relations.project_anchor: Woman/mourning/tomb/absence/return is modeled as witness function, not identity proof.
new_relations.source_direction: Project mourning/tomb language and Gospel narratives are compared as sequences.
new_relations.boundary: Gospel accounts differ; the combined chain is an intertextual synthesis, not one scene or modern identity map.

project_sequence: loss; boundary witnesses; changed evidence; recognition
biblical_sequence: women witness burial; stone; return; moved stone; absent body; rising testimony
relation_argument.maximum_claim: The texts support women-as-witness around burial, absence and resurrection traditions.
relation_argument.why_it_matters: Makes mourning witnesses evidence-bearing participants rather than background.

new_relations.project_anchor: Tomb, Gardener, recognition/return and Father co-occur as project motifs requiring strict boundaries.
new_relations.source_direction: The project cluster is compared later with John's dense sequence.
new_relations.boundary: Mary's gardener misrecognition and Jesus' Father language do not identify a modern figure with Jesus.

project_sequence: absence; blocked recognition; Gardener; recognition; Father
biblical_sequence: weeping at tomb; gardener mistake; recognition; ascending to Father
relation_argument.maximum_claim: John 20 is a dense tomb-to-gardener-to-recognition-to-Father comparator.
relation_argument.why_it_matters: Provides a whole-scene comparator while preserving identities.

new_relations.project_anchor: Gate, mourning woman, Son/death and return are treated as separate functions.
new_relations.source_direction: The project motif cluster is compared later with Luke's gate scene.
new_relations.boundary: The widow's son is not a prediction or identity template for a modern Son narrative.

project_sequence: gate boundary; mourning; son; restoration
biblical_sequence: city gate; widow; dead only son; weeping; son raised and returned
relation_argument.maximum_claim: Luke supplies a compact gate+mourning+dead-son+restoration sequence.
relation_argument.why_it_matters: Strengthens Gate/return without messianic identity mapping.

new_relations.project_anchor: A Hebrew-Bible mourning-to-return comparator is needed apart from Gospel tomb scenes.
new_relations.source_direction: Project mourning/return language is compared with Jeremiah's maternal lament.
new_relations.boundary: The passage concerns Rachel/children and restoration, not a modern biography.

project_sequence: loss; lament preserved; future hope
biblical_sequence: bitter weeping; children no more; promised return
relation_argument.maximum_claim: The text supports a mourning-to-absence-to-future-return structure.
relation_argument.why_it_matters: Prevents return grammar from depending only on Christian tomb narratives.
